Subject: Regional failover SLAs, credit cap and maintenance phasing

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Based on our discussion I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table for the Order Form / SLA section so your procurement and ops teams have something concrete to work with. High level items we talked through: regional failover behavior, limits on aggregate service credits, and splitting scheduled maintenance into phased windows to avoid cross-region impacts.

Key proposal (first pass):
- Regional failover: Redwood will route traffic to a secondary region within the same cloud provider; for regional outages where traffic is successfully served from secondary region, availability shortfalls will be measured per-region and credits applied to the affected region rather than globally.
- Credit cap: 12 months rolling cap equal to 75% of the monthly recurring charges for the affected environment; for multi-region deployments the cap is per-region, capped at 150% of single-region MRC across all regions.
- Response times: P1 response target 15 minutes (ack), P2 1 hour, with remediation SLAs defined in the appendix.
- Maintenance phasing: scheduled maintenance impacting an entire region will be split into three phased windows per region over a 72-hour period to avoid simultaneous multi-region impact; emergency maintenance exceptions still apply.

I've attached a marked-up Order Form excerpt and a regional-failover matrix that maps credit calculation examples for a multi-region deployment. If that structure looks reasonable we can send a tracked-change version to legal for formal redlines.

Next steps:
1) Confirm this approach with Ops/Procurement at Acme.
2) I'll loop in Laura and Kimberly for the tracked redlines.
3) If agreed, we prepare an Order Form with tracked changes and a DocuSign-ready appendix.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick write-up. A few clarifying points from our side before we escalate to legal: 

1) For regional failover, our concern is around data locality and latency-sensitive workloads. If we switch traffic to a secondary region, we need a guarantee that session affinity and key-value caching behave consistently (not just "served" from another region). Can you outline what operational constraints apply and whether there are any performance SLOs for failover traffic?

2) Credit cap: 75% MRC per region seems reasonable but procurement will push back on the 150% aggregate cap for multi-region customers — they want to know worst-case recourse. Can you provide a worked example for a 3-region deployment (eu/us/apac) showing how credits would accumulate?

3) Maintenance phasing: the phased approach is good. Ops would like a shorter maximum blackout window per region (no more than 4 hours contiguous for planned work) and advance notice of 14 days for non-emergency maintenance.

If you can get Laura/Kimberly to include concrete clause language and the 3-region credit example we can expedite the redline.

Best,
Jane Smith
Sr. IT Procurement Manager | Acme Solutions

Jordan / team —

Draft wording below you can paste into the Order Form (tracked changes included in the attached):

1) Failover and consistency: "Redwood will provide regional failover by routing traffic to a designated secondary region under the same cloud provider. Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to preserve session affinity and in-memory KV cache state; however, in the event of a regional evacuation the Parties acknowledge that transient cache misses and warm-up latency may occur. Redwood warrants that failover routing will preserve request ordering for individual client sessions to the extent permitted by underlying transport. Performance during failover is not subject to the Availability target but will be measured for informational SLO purposes and will not generate service credits unless underlying Availability thresholds are breached."

2) Worked credit example (3-region):
- Scenario numbers: monthly recurring charge (MRC) per region = $100k.
- Measured downtime for region A in month = 20 hours (cumulative) => Availability falls into the slab that yields 30% of that region's monthly MRC as credit for that month ($30k).
- If region B experiences 10 hours in same rolling 30-day window => 15% credit for region B ($15k).
- Aggregate paid credits across regions in a rolling 12-month window will be capped at 75% of the single-region annualized MRC (i.e., 0.75 * 12 * $100k = $900k) and further bounded at 150% of single-region MRC in any single month (i.e., cap of $150k per month). This creates an annual cap and a per-month safety valve.

3) Maintenance phasing and notice: "Planned maintenance that may impact Availability will be scheduled in phased regional windows. No planned maintenance window will exceed four (4) contiguous hours per region without Customer consent. Redwood will provide at least fourteen (14) calendar days' notice for non-emergency planned maintenance. Urgent or emergency maintenance may be performed with as much notice as practicable and will be documented in the incident ledger."

Attached: redwood_sla_response_table.pdf (response ladders by priority) and a tracked changes docx with the above wording inserted. I kept the credit math conservative to address procurement pushback — they can see the 3-region example and the annual cap.

LMK if you'd like a softer credit cap (we can move annual cap to 100% of single-region annual MRC) — that might get procurement to sign faster.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
